messages.content: Get the protein sequence of human HbA1c, normal hemoglobin, and rat hemoglobin and their 3D models

function.name: protein_info_get_sequence_and_3D
function.description: Retrive the sequence and 3D models of proteins. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

model_3d.description: Set true to get 3D model of the protein.

message.reasoning:
The user wants the protein sequence of human HbA1c (which is glycated hemoglobin A1c), normal hemoglobin (presumably human adult hemoglobin alpha and beta chains?), and rat hemoglobin. They also want 3D models. We need to use the provided function `protein_info_get_sequence_and_3D`. We can call it multiple times with different protein names. For each call we provide the protein_name and set model_3d to true.

We should ask clarifying question? The user didn't specify which subunits or isoforms. But they said "human HbA1c, normal hemoglobin, and rat hemoglobin". So likely they want sequences for human HbA1c (glycated form of human adult hemoglobin). Normal hemoglobin could refer to human adult hemoglobin (HbA) alpha and beta chains. Rat hemoglobin might refer to rat adult hemoglobin (alpha and beta chains). We can retrieve sequences for human alpha chain, human beta chain, rat alpha chain, rat beta chain. For HbA1c, it's basically the same as human adult hemoglobin but with glycation at N-terminal valine of beta chain. Sequence wise it's identical except post-translational modification. So we can just give the sequence of human beta chain. But maybe we can mention glycation site.

Thus we will call the function for:

- Human hemoglobin alpha chain
- Human hemoglobin beta chain
- Rat hemoglobin alpha chain
- Rat hemoglobin beta chain

Also maybe include the full tetramer? But we can provide separate chains.

We'll call the function four times.
